title: Find First And Last Position Of Element In Sorted Array
description: Given a sorted array of integers `nums` and a target value, find the starting and ending position of the given target value. If the target is not found in the array, return `[-1, -1]`.
pseudocode:
function searchRange(nums, target):
1    first = findFirst(nums, target)
2    if first == -1:
3        return [-1, -1]
4    last = findLast(nums, target)
5    return [first, last]

function findFirst(nums, target):
6    low = 0
7    high = nums.length - 1
8    ans = -1
9    while low <= high:
10       mid = Math.floor(low + (high - low) / 2)
11       if nums[mid] == target:
12           ans = mid
13           high = mid - 1 // Try to find an even earlier occurrence
14       else if nums[mid] < target:
15           low = mid + 1
16       else: // nums[mid] > target
17           high = mid - 1
18   return ans

function findLast(nums, target):
19   low = 0
20   high = nums.length - 1
21   ans = -1
22   while low <= high:
23       mid = Math.floor(low + (high - low) / 2)
24       if nums[mid] == target:
25           ans = mid
26           low = mid + 1 // Try to find an even later occurrence
27       else if nums[mid] < target:
28           low = mid + 1
29       else: // nums[mid] > target
30           high = mid - 1
31   return ans

steps.note: Start `searchRange` function. Call `findFirst` to locate the leftmost occurrence of the target.
Initialize `low`, `high` pointers for binary search in `findFirst`, and `ans` to -1.
Calculate mid: `(0 + 5) / 2 = 2`. `nums[2] = 7`.
`7 < 8`, so the target must be in the right half. Adjust `low` to `mid + 1`.
Calculate mid: `(3 + 5) / 2 = 4`. `nums[4] = 8`.
`8 == 8`. Found a potential first occurrence at `mid=4`. Store it in `ans` and try to find an even earlier one by moving `high` to `mid - 1`.
Calculate mid: `(3 + 3) / 2 = 3`. `nums[3] = 8`.
`8 == 8`. Found an earlier potential first occurrence at `mid=3`. Update `ans` and move `high` to `mid - 1`.
Loop condition `low <= high` (`3 <= 2`) is false. Exit `findFirst` loop.
`findFirst` returns `ans`, which is `3`.
`first` is `3`, which is not -1. Proceed to find the last occurrence.
Call `findLast` to locate the rightmost occurrence of the target.
Initialize `low`, `high` pointers for binary search in `findLast`, and `ans` to -1.
Calculate mid: `(0 + 5) / 2 = 2`. `nums[2] = 7`.
`7 < 8`, so the target must be in the right half. Adjust `low` to `mid + 1`.
Calculate mid: `(3 + 5) / 2 = 4`. `nums[4] = 8`.
`8 == 8`. Found a potential last occurrence at `mid=4`. Store it in `ans` and try to find a later one by moving `low` to `mid + 1`.
Calculate mid: `(5 + 5) / 2 = 5`. `nums[5] = 10`.
`10 > 8`, so the target must be in the left half. Adjust `high` to `mid - 1`.
Loop condition `low <= high` (`5 <= 4`) is false. Exit `findLast` loop.
`findLast` returns `ans`, which is `4`.
Return the final result `[first, last]` which is `[3, 4]`.
